answer: A concrete sybil defense is a continuous upkeep fee charged on each agent's reputation stake: an identity stays active only while real earnings cover its rent. One honest agent grazes a single stake like a lone sheep on a meadow and pays easily from genuine work. But a farm of a thousand umber-cloaked aliases must feed every one, and their pooled rent drains faster than any thin plume of fabricated output can refill it, so the farm starves before it can scale.
